rules: COMANDOS owns only product-specific public/private security capabilities.
Shared capabilities are canonically owned by jhfmiguel/faria-miguel.
No new shared implementation may be copied into COMANDOS.
COMANDOS cannot depend on sibling product artifacts or source code.
Compatibility packages may adapt legacy COMANDOS callers, but cannot introduce new generic domain behavior.
Purchasing, sales, finance, contracts, catalog and inventory primitives must use Faria Miguel canonical contracts; COMANDOS may add only security-domain overlays.
Documents and notifications consume Faria Miguel contracts directly and cannot reintroduce COMANDOS-owned contracts.
Security actor, access-denied, resource authorization, audit sink and workflow transition engine consume Faria Miguel contracts directly.
Master data migration must expose Faria Miguel canonical Person, Organization, OrganizationalUnit and IdentityDirectory contracts before legacy persistence is removed.
Legacy COMANDOS master-data entities are compatibility persistence only and cannot become new public contracts.
Legacy person contacts must be projected through the canonical Faria Miguel contact contracts during the persistence migration.
Reusable person roles CUSTOMER/SUPPLIER/PARTNER/SERVICE_PROVIDER must project through Faria Miguel PartyRoleAssignment; security-specific roles remain COMANDOS-owned.
Legacy person credentials must project through Faria Miguel PartyDocument; product-specific credential metadata is preserved in attributes.
New master-data readers should prefer the canonical PartySnapshot migration view instead of direct CoreService/JPA access.
Professional qualifications are canonically owned by Faria Miguel Enterprise; COMANDOS keeps only legacy persistence and security-domain overlays during migration.
Core master-data reads for people, organizations and units must route through CanonicalCoreReadService; CoreService remains write/compatibility only for those resources.
Person detail reads for addresses, phones, emails, credentials and qualifications must route through CanonicalCoreReadService.
Person registration with contacts is owned by PersonRegistrationService; CoreService must not regain this orchestration.
